summary: The hierarchical BoQ breakdown-% work and the Excel importer are solid: computeHierarchicalAmount/insertLineItems correctly walk the parent chain to the root 'Main' item per the Owner's exact formula, detect circular/missing parent references before any row is written, and insertLineItems does a proper topological (parent-before-child) batch insert so parentLineItemId gets real DB ids; diffLineItems is a clean, hierarchy-aware pure extraction with good unit-test coverage; the Excel importer's dot-delimited item-code parent inference is a reasonable, well-scoped reuse of the existing spreadsheet-parsing pipeline; RLS on the two new tables correctly follows the established direct-org_id + EXISTS-join pattern from 0101_wave115; all new API routes call requireAuth() and are tenant-scoped. However, construction-valuation-service.ts's generateInterimBill() has an undisclosed, real correctness gap for a GST-compliance platform: the invoice line items it builds (billable BoQ lines plus a negative 'Retention held' line) never set taxTemplateId, and erp-invoicing-service.ts's computeInvoiceTotals() only applies tax when a line explicitly carries a taxTemplateId with no company/customer-level fallback -- so every interim/RA bill generated through this new feature will silently post with zero GST/tax, and GenerateInterimBillInput doesn't even expose a field to set one. This wasn't caught by the pure-function unit tests (which don't assert on tax) and isn't mentioned anywhere in PROGRESS.md's Remaining section, unlike the migration-not-applied and get_advisors gaps which were disclosed. Separately, modeling retention as a negative invoice line reduces the invoice's taxable value rather than leaving it as a payment-term holdback on the full taxed amount, which compounds the tax problem once taxTemplateId is wired in and should be revisited together. Neither issue is a security hole and the migration/RLS/tenant-isolation work is sound, but shipping a billing feature that produces zero-tax invoices by default on a compliance-tracking product is a material gap that should be fixed (or at minimum explicitly flagged to the Owner and PROGRESS.md) before this goes to human sign-off.
issues: construction-valuation-service.ts generateInterimBill(): invoice line items passed to createSalesInvoice never set taxTemplateId, and computeInvoiceTotals() in erp-invoicing-service.ts only computes tax for lines that carry one (no default/fallback) -- every interim/RA bill generated by this feature posts with $0 GST/tax and GenerateInterimBillInput has no field to supply one. Not disclosed in PROGRESS.md.

Retention is modeled as a negative invoice line item (rate: -retentionAmount), which reduces the invoice's taxable subtotal rather than being a payment-term holdback on the full taxed gross amount -- once tax is wired in, this will also understate GST collected by the retention percentage; worth revisiting together with the tax gap.

Minor/pre-existing-pattern: interim bill numbering uses max(billNumber)+1 read-then-insert with no unique constraint on (projectId, billNumber) in the migration, so concurrent generateInterimBill calls for the same project could produce duplicate bill numbers -- matches an existing convention elsewhere in the codebase (erpSalesInvoices.invoiceNumber) so not a new pattern, but worth a follow-up if concurrent billing is a realistic scenario.

Migration drizzle/0265_construction_boq_hierarchy_interim_billing.sql is hand-written (not drizzle-kit generated output) due to a pre-existing gap in drizzle/meta/ snapshots, and per the worker's own PROGRESS.md has not been applied to any live Supabase project nor had get_advisors(security) run against it post-migration -- correctly flagged by the worker as needing explicit Owner sign-off before merge, consistent with this being tier2.
